subject: Observability collection patterns for FinTrust private deployment — network & SIEM constraints
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morris <alice@fintrust.com>, security@fintrust.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability collection patterns for FinTrust private deployment — initial diagram and questions

Hi Alice / FinTrust security team,

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, we're drafting a short playbook for how Redwood will collect and export logs/metrics/traces from the private VPC deployment you plan to host in your Azure subscription. The diagram attached is an early sketch — please treat as draft (edge-collector-networking-diagram.png).

Key open questions we want to confirm before the runbook:
- Allowed outbound destinations/ports from the customer VPC (we asked for CIDR/IP allowlist for any third-party forwarder).
- Whether you prefer: (A) syslog-over-TLS (RFC 5425) to your Splunk HEC collector, or (B) OTLP over TLS to your in-house OpenTelemetry collector, or (C) encrypted S3/GCS drop with server-side encryption + KMS.
- Tracing: recommended sampling rates for user-facing vs internal system spans and whether PII should be stripped at the collector.
- Retention & evidence: minimum retention for audit logs you need us to preserve in the export bundle (e.g., auth events, request IDs).

Attachments: edge-collector-networking-diagram.png, fintrust-siem-reqs.xlsx (blank worksheet with fields we typically need).

Proposed next steps: you share any CIDR/IP restrictions and preferred mode (A/B/C) and we’ll produce a short runbook + smoke test checklist.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Alice Morris <alice@fintrust.com>

Date: 2027-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability collection patterns for FinTrust private deployment — initial diagram and questions

Sean — thanks for the diagram and call summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Outbound network: we will only open egress to an allowlist of IP:port pairs. We cannot allow arbitrary outbound to new hosts. Please provide the IPs/hostnames your collectors need to reach (or indicate that you support connecting to an endpoint we host internally).
- Preferred transport: our security team prefers OTLP over TLS to our in-house collector where possible. If you cannot natively speak OTLP, we can accept syslog-over-TLS but it must terminate on a dedicated forwarder with mTLS.
- S3 drop: acceptable only for non-sensitive telemetry (aggregated metrics, sampled traces) and must be to a bucket we control with SSE-KMS and restricted access.
- PII handling: all request payloads that contain PII must be redacted before export. We expect a configuration flag or rewrite rule at the collector.
- Retention: we require 90 days for auth/audit logs in raw form and 365 days for aggregated metrics. Evidence format should be CSV or JSON; we prefer a manifest index for any bulk exports.

I'll loop in Ian from CloudPartner (our integrator) to confirm the OTLP endpoint details and cert rotation processes.

Best,
Alice
Alice Morris
Director, Security Operations — FinTrust Bank
alice@fintrust.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morris <alice@fintrust.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability collection patterns for FinTrust private deployment — initial diagram and questions

Thanks Alice — clear constraints, good call. Sean / team, putting together an implementation approach that fits FinTrust constraints. High-level proposal below: 

1) Collector topology (recommended):
   - Local edge agent inside FinTrust VPC (Fluent Bit + OpenTelemetry Collector sidecar). Fluent Bit handles logs, OTel collects traces/metrics.
   - Local aggregator (customer-controlled VM/container) performs PII redaction rules (configurable regex) before any export.
   - Export modes supported: OTLP over mTLS to FinTrust internal collector (preferred), or syslog-over-TLS to a Splunk forwarder listening on an allowlisted IP.

2) Networking & security notes:
   - Mutual TLS for all connections from our agents to any FinTrust endpoint; certs rotated via ACME or manual provisioning per their SA policy.
   - Egress: agents only speak to configured endpoints; we will provide an explicit list of IPs/hostnames for firewall rules.
   - Fallback: if OTLP is blocked, system will failover to encrypted S3 drop with server-side KMS and pre-signed upload URL; bucket policies lock access to the FinTrust account.

3) Tracing & sampling:
   - Default sampling: 1% global with 100% for error spans and 10% for transactions flagged as high-priority (payment / auth flows).
   - Option to purge or hash PII fields at collector using pipeline processors; config will be exposed in runbook.

4) Data retention & evidence:
   - We will produce a daily manifest (JSON) listing exported files, sha256 checksums, and record counts.
   - For audits, we can produce a time-bound export package (CSV + JSON manifest) covering requested windows.

Attachments: runbook-obsv-smoke-tests.md (draft checklist).

Next actions: Sean / Laura to produce the allowlist IPs and a minimal config YAML for the Fluent Bit + OTEL collector. Mina, can you draft the runbook and smoke-test steps?

— Vanessa

Subject: Fwd: Observability collection patterns for FinTrust private deployment — integration & runbook request

Ian — forwarding the thread. FinTrust prefers OTLP to their collector and strict allowlist egress. We need CloudPartner to confirm the following so we can finalize the runbook: 

- OTLP endpoint hostname/IP and port (we need stable IPs for firewall rules or confirmation that FinTrust will permit DNS-based hosts).
- TLS/mTLS requirements: will CloudPartner host a client cert bundle or should we provision certs via ACME? Describe cert rotation cadence and automation options.
- Any vendor-side preprocessors you recommend for removing PII at ingress (we prefer OTel processors but open to CloudPartner recommendations).
- A short validation plan: handshake test, span propagation verification (trace ids), and log-to-trace correlation smoke tests.

Please reply with a short bulleted plan; we’ll slot this into the runbook and share with FinTrust's security team.

Thanks — Mina
